inspiration: Armour is shown by swapping one material texture per body part to a tier (leather, chain, plate), chosen from the slot the server reports, then tinting it. Recreate as tier swaps per body part with our own palettes and armour names.

Coordinate conversion is kept in one crate (eq-client-axes), so every position, rotation and triangle converts from one definition. Keep that boundary idea for our camera and world maths; this is cross-link camera.
Terrain is loaded as three kinds of material: repeating ground, transparent cut-outs and static props (trees, buildings). Recreate the three material classes with our own art.
Water and lava are zone regions, not meshes: a region type fills part of the zone. Recreate as data-driven fill regions with our own water look and animation.
Appearance updates from the network drive a model's posture for known characters. Recreate as a mapping from an appearance or stance state to a pose, with our own pose set.
The HUD keeps a spell-gem bar and a memorised-spell list fed from typed events. Recreate the hotbar pattern with our own icons; this is the hud-ui cross-link.

briefs.label: Tiered body armour swap
briefs.why: One base body can show progression by changing the material set per body part, which is cheap and readable at a distance.
briefs.keep: One texture per body part; tiers as named material sets; tint on top
briefs.change: Our own tiers (cloth, scale, crystal, or similar); per-faction tint; our own proportions and ornament

briefs.keep: Region type decides the fill; the region is a data record, not a mesh
